data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'jawharah' meaning 'grain' or 'seed'. In Islamic tradition, Johar represents the concept of self-renewal and growth, as well as the idea of planting seeds of good deeds that will bear fruit in the future. The name Johar carries the meaning “Grain, seed” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Johar usually hope their child will grow to embody grain, seed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
